Official5.1.1 shipped toolbox exact proof tuple storage lookup

interpretations.direct-extra-url: Pinned SDK compatibility observation: direct acquisition ignores a valid inactive certifierUrl and returns the exact direct certificate without HTTP. BRC100 marks the URL required for issuance but does not independently prohibit it on direct requests.
interpretations.issuance-direct-fields: Pinned SDK compatibility observation: issuance validation rejects populated direct-only fields before HTTP; this is not asserted to be a universal BRC100 mutual-exclusion rule. The fixed request contains all five direct-only fields, so it does not establish individual rejection of every such field.
interpretations.empty-filters: Pinned SDK/storage interpretation: empty certifiers or types arrays impose no constraint in that dimension. Compare exact authenticated baseline plus fresh fixtures, not an assumed empty wallet.
interpretations.proof-tuple: The full supplied certificate tuple (type, serial, issuer, subject, revocation outpoint and signature) identifies one stored certificate. Four negatives change only issuer, serial, subject or a syntactically valid signature; successful designated-verifier selective disclosure is a required control.
interpretations.revocation: The real existing boundary output is cryptographically bound as a certificate revocation reference. This module does not spend it or claim any revocation-state checking by acquisition, proof, or discovery.

invariants: Four issuer-signed, independently decrypted external fixtures with fixed types, subjects, serials, fields and an ancestry-bound revocation outpoint.
Three successful direct acquisitions are separately required; failure cannot be hidden by passing negative calls.
Every inventory is complete below limit10000, unique by certificate tuple, and compared by all signed certificate fields.
Before/after inventories prove rejected mutations and proof mismatches do not alter public certificate state.
All calls retain exact arguments, errors, submission boundaries and controlled-HTTP boundaries.
Cleanup affirmatively relinquishes only the three added certificates and restores the entire authenticated baseline.
No private wallet storage mutation, no new funding, no HTTP issuance, no browser restart.

The parent binds exact boundary anchor and native identity, full scoped route and submission prefix/range to independent global ledgers, and every unique /certificate-state endpoint attempt across the entire run. OPTIONS and authentication traffic count as HTTP even without a handler receipt.
remainingUnqualified: Wrong authenticated issuance peer identity; new authenticated peer fixture required.
Extra field key, empty/duplicate disclosure field and repeated relinquishment policies require separately admitted compatibility interpretations.
Inventory restart persistence is not established by this module.
Revocation spent-state semantics across acquisition/proof/discovery and malformed revocation reference require a separate frozen policy and controlled chain transition.
Multiple-certifier discovery, malicious overlay certificate/keyring records, and discovery permission default/explicit consent require source-bound trust/lookup/UI fixtures.
